source_refs.note: Exercise 3.5, Question 2 (i)-(iii): piecewise and absolute-value integrals; book p. 101. Key on p. 300 under 'Exercise 3.2'; (iii) is labelled a second '(ii)'.

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Evaluate the following definite integral: \(\int_{-1}^{1} f(x)\,dx\), where \(f(x) = \begin{cases} 5 - 3x & \text{if } x \leq 0 \\ 5 + 3x & \text{if } x > 0 \end{cases}\)
blocks.explanation:
A piecewise function: one formula left of 0, another right of 0.
Split the interval at the corner point \(x = 0\) (Property III) and integrate each formula on its own piece.
Add the two results.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 5 - 3x\) for \(x \leq 0\), \(f(x) = 5 + 3x\) for \(x > 0\).
To find: \(\int_{-1}^{1} f(x)\,dx\).
Method: Property III \(\int_a^b f = \int_a^c f + \int_c^b f\) with \(c = 0\), where the formula changes.

Split at \(x = 0\)
\[\int_{-1}^{1} f(x)\,dx = \int_{-1}^{0} (5 - 3x)\,dx\]
\[+ \int_{0}^{1} (5 + 3x)\,dx\]
Why: on \([-1, 0]\) the first rule holds, on \((0, 1]\) the second. One point does not change an integral.

Left piece
\[\left[5x - \dfrac{3x^2}{2}\right]_{-1}^{0} = 0 - \left(-5 - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{13}{2}\]
Why: at \(x = -1\): \(5(-1) - \frac{3}{2}(1) = -\frac{13}{2}\); subtracting a negative adds.

Right piece
\[\left[5x + \dfrac{3x^2}{2}\right]_{0}^{1} = 5 + \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{13}{2}\]
Why: power rule; the value at 0 is 0.

Add
\[\int_{-1}^{1} f(x)\,dx = \dfrac{13}{2} + \dfrac{13}{2} = 13\]
Why: Property III.

Check
\[f(-x) = 5 + 3x = f(x)\ \ (x > 0)\]
Why: \(f\) is even (its graph is the V-shape \(5 + 3|x|\)), so the two halves must be equal, as found. The answer key also prints 13.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Evaluate the following definite integral: \(\int_{-3}^{5} f(x)\,dx\), where \(f(x) = |x - 4| + |x|\)
blocks.explanation:
A sum of two absolute values; each changes its formula where its inside is zero.
Corner points: \(x = 4\) and \(x = 0\). Split \([-3, 5]\) at 0 and 4 and write \(f\) without bars on each piece.
Integrate the three pieces and add.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = |x - 4| + |x|\) on \([-3, 5]\).
To find: \(\int_{-3}^{5} f(x)\,dx\).
Method: \(|u| = u\) when \(u \geq 0\) and \(|u| = -u\) when \(u < 0\); split at the zeros of \(x - 4\) and \(x\) (Property III), as in Example 50.

Second piece
\[\int_{0}^{4} 4\,dx = \Big[4x\Big]_{0}^{4} = 16\]
Why: constant integrand; area of a rectangle \(4 \times 4\).

Add
\[\int_{-3}^{5} f(x)\,dx = 21 + 16 + 5 = 42\]
Why: Property III.

Check by triangles
\[\int_{-3}^{5} |x - 4|\,dx = \tfrac{1}{2}(7)(7) + \tfrac{1}{2}(1)(1) = 25\]
\[\int_{-3}^{5} |x|\,dx = \tfrac{1}{2}(3)(3) + \tfrac{1}{2}(5)(5) = 17\]
Why: the graph of each absolute value is a V made of two triangles; \(25 + 17 = 42\). The key also prints 42.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Evaluate the following definite integral: \(\int_{-3}^{4} |4 - x^2|\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
An absolute value of \(4 - x^2\), which changes sign at \(x = \pm 2\).
On \([-2, 2]\) we have \(4 - x^2 \geq 0\); outside it, \(4 - x^2 < 0\). Split \([-3, 4]\) at \(-2\) and \(2\).
Integrate three pieces and add.
steps:
Given: \(\int_{-3}^{4} |4 - x^2|\,dx\).
To find: its value.
Method: find where \(4 - x^2 = 0\) (\(x = \pm 2\)), remove the bars on each piece, then Property III.

Middle piece
\[\left[4x - \dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^{2} = \left(8 - \dfrac{8}{3}\right) - \left(-8 + \dfrac{8}{3}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{16}{3} + \dfrac{16}{3} = \dfrac{32}{3}\]
Why: power rule; the integrand is even, so this is twice the value on \([0, 2]\).

Last piece
\[\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3} - 4x\right]_{2}^{4} = \left(\dfrac{64}{3} - 16\right) - \left(\dfrac{8}{3} - 8\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{16}{3} + \dfrac{16}{3} = \dfrac{32}{3}\]
Why: power rule.

Add
\[\dfrac{7}{3} + \dfrac{32}{3} + \dfrac{32}{3} = \dfrac{71}{3}\]
Why: Property III.

Check
\[\int_{-3}^{4} (4 - x^2)\,dx = -\dfrac{7}{3}\]
\[-\dfrac{7}{3} + 2\left(\dfrac{7}{3} + \dfrac{32}{3}\right) = \dfrac{71}{3} \;\checkmark\]
Why: without bars the two outer pieces count as negative; adding them back twice turns them positive. The key prints \(\frac{71}{3}\).

blocks.text: The answer key labels this answer '(ii)' a second time (it reads 2. (i) 13, (ii) 42, (ii) \(\frac{71}{3}\)). The third answer belongs to part (iii); its value \(\frac{71}{3}\) is correct.
